clue.text: Fellow leads firm sailor on board

parts.note: CO is the usual abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: being on a ship means sitting inside its letters, so this word puts the sailor within the vessel

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the vessel one is aboard
a tar is an old word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A company recruits a seaman to join the crew of its ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' is the stock crossword way of placing something inside SS, the steamship.
explanation.definitionFit: Co-stars share top billing in a film or play, so each is one of several fellow leading actors.

clue.text: Trick by one stealing gold crown

indicators.note: the trick and one steal the gold, taking it inside them

parts.note: a con is a swindle or trick
OR is the heraldic word for gold
A means one, as in a single item

explanation.surface: A swindler makes off with a gold crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A corona is a crown-like structure or ring, from the Latin word for a wreath.

clue.text: Chairs in cars

definitions.meaning: sedan chairs, enclosed seats carried on poles
the American word for saloon cars

explanation.surface: Seats inside motor vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedan names both an old carried seat for one passenger and an enclosed motor vehicle with a separate boot.

clue.text: Adult delivery men carry ones defections

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult

indicators.note: the delivery men carry the letters within them

parts.note: posties is British slang for postmen
A is one, so AS is more than one

explanation.surface: Grown-up postmen are carrying some parcels for traitors.
explanation.walkthrough: Posties is a British informal word for postal workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is the abandoning of a faith or party, a desertion, so apostasies are acts of disloyal abandonment.

clue.text: Room key

definitions.meaning: the long key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: A key that opens a room.
explanation.definitionFit: Space is free area to move in, and the space bar is the widest keyboard button.

clue.text: Relative size has girl worried

indicators.note: something worried has been pulled about and tugged, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member's measurements have left a young woman anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relative' looks like a family member but describes size: the anagram of HASGIRL, from 'worried', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Largish describes a size that is big only by comparison, a relative judgment of bulk rather than an absolute measure.

clue.text: 508 (roughly) reject play on words? Relax!

indicators.note: roughly means in rough, shaken-up order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: 50 is L in Roman numerals and 8 is the word eight

indicators.note: to reject something is to throw it back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A number, 508 more or less, turns down wordplay and tells the solver to calm down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' shuffles L plus EIGHT into LIGHTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighten up is an informal instruction to stop being so serious and take things easier.

clue.text: Call inquiringly?

indicators.note: the question mark warns that inquiringly must be read oddly, as 'in quiringly', so the call is in what follows 'in'

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark makes the solver split the last word as 'in' plus QUIRINGLY: the call sits in those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring someone is British for to telephone or phone them, so a ring is a call.

clue.text: 1 + 500 + 10 + 50 etc translated into personal speech

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
the Roman numeral D is five hundred
ten written with the letters I and O for its digits
the Roman numeral L is fifty

indicators.note: translated means carried into another form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A string of numbers, rendered in another language, becomes someone's own way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: The digits of 10 are read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiolect is the speech habits peculiar to one individual, their own personal language.

clue.text: Wonderful cat, just not ordinary

parts.note: to cat is slang for to vomit, as to heave also means

indicators.note: not means without, so the ordinary letter is dropped

parts.note: only means just, as in merely
O is the abbreviation for ordinary, from O level

explanation.surface: A remarkable feline, though nothing out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: Cat as a verb, meaning to vomit, is British slang that the surface hides behind the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavenly is used informally for something delightful, as if from paradise, so it means marvellous.

clue.text: Start to roll a board game's ten-sided die — set?

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of roll is taken

parts.note: in role-playing board games such as Dungeons and Dragons a ten-sided die is called a d10, written here as D-I-O

explanation.surface: Instructions from a games night: begin by rolling the ten-sided die, then ask whether everyone is ready.
explanation.walkthrough: The 10 of D10 is read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: A wireless receiver is often called a radio set, so set with a question mark hints at that example.

clue.text: Excited at nearing country

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and jumbled, so these are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled to be approaching a destination abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a nation in South America, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: A fraction enter the inn drunk, then run away

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so these letters are thrown into disorder
something sent away is no longer there, so this letter is removed from the mix

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
R is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A tipsy customer stumbles into the pub and then bolts.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ENTERTHEINN from 'drunk' has one letter too many; 'run away' takes out R.
explanation.definitionFit: One part in nineteen equal parts is a nineteenth, a fraction just like a half or a tenth.

clue.text: Learner breaks sports equipment like this?

indicators.note: to break something is to split it open, so the learner letter goes into the middle

parts.note: a cue is the stick used in snooker and billiards
L is the learner abbreviation, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A novice smashes some kit at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points at the very thing the solver is reading: this sentence is itself an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The words in front of the solver form a crossword clue, so the answer names what this item is.

clue.text: Shape of diamond strangely altered to save money, including copper

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the copper symbol goes inside
strangely means oddly, so these letters are arranged in an odd new way

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
M abbreviates money, and to save it is to keep it in with the letters of altered
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A gem's shape was oddly changed to cut costs, and copper was added.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to save money' looks like a phrase for thrift, but it keeps M among the letters 'strangely' rearranges into EMERALDT; 'including' then puts CU into them.
explanation.definitionFit: An emerald cut is a rectangular step-faceted style in which gemstones, including diamonds, are shaped.

clue.text: Huge shock! Nostromo alien — can none get lost?

indicators.note: a shock of hair is a wild tangle, so these letters are tousled into a new order
letters that get lost vanish from the mix, so these are taken out of the fodder

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
anagram fodder taken as written
anagram fodder taken as written
letters removed from the fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Fans of the film Alien gasp: the Nostromo's creature defeated, and is nobody lost?
explanation.walkthrough: 'shock' rearranges NOSTROMOALIENCAN and 'get lost' removes N, O, N and E from that pool. The Nostromo is the spaceship in Alien.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomical figures are of a vast, star-distance scale, so the word is used loosely for anything enormous.

clue.text: Historical role player's career not flourishing

indicators.note: to flourish something is to wave it about, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: An actor in period dramas finds their profession failing to thrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flourishing' looks like the opposite of 'not', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A re-enactor dresses up to play a part in a staged recreation of a past event, such as a battle.

clue.text: Vague sense to gather up American lubricant

indicators.note: to gather is to collect in, so the sense word contains the lubricant

parts.note: nous is common sense

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means read from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: lube is an American shortening of lubricant

explanation.surface: Imprecise reasoning about collecting some US oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Nebulous means hazy or ill-defined, like a cloud of gas, and so is a synonym of unclear.

clue.text: A shoe size bigger than 9C, say, on conference goer

indicators.note: say means spoken, so the answer is the shoe size said out

parts.note: a size 10D is bigger than 9C, read out as 'a ten dee'

explanation.surface: A delegate at a meeting has larger feet than average.
explanation.walkthrough: American shoe sizes pair a number with a width letter, so 10D is a step up from 9C.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendee is someone present at an event, such as a delegate at a meeting.

clue.text: Some expert activity, right, like hang-gliding?

indicators.note: activity means busy movement, so these letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A few skilled people pursue some pastime, and hang-gliding is a fair example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' and 'activity' read as ordinary words, but 'activity' rearranges SOMEEXPERT into EXTREMESPO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hang-gliding is a risky adrenaline pursuit, an example of the dangerous category of recreation.

clue.text: Because I'm travelling skywards, the speed of light is enormous

parts.note: cos is an informal clipping of because

indicators.note: in a down entry, going skywards means reading upwards, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: c is the physics symbol for the speed of light

explanation.surface: Physics boast: as I rise into space, light is extremely fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Cosmic means relating to the universe, and so, by extension, vast in scale or immeasurable.

clue.text: Hit sung loudly after dropping out

indicators.note: dropping means letting go, so the word that follows is removed

parts.note: belted out means sang loudly and forcefully

explanation.surface: A chart-topper's chorus was sung with gusto after a dropout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropping' removes the word 'out' itself from the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To belt someone is to strike them hard, so belted is a synonym of struck.

clue.text: Took drugs, thought to blow money

indicators.note: to blow cash is to spend it all, so the money letter disappears

parts.note: mused means pondered or thought

explanation.surface: Someone reflected on squandering their cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To use is slang for taking illegal drugs habitually, so the past tense fits a past habit.

clue.text: Dessert from South Africa prepared in a globe

parts.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa

indicators.note: food prepared is made up from its ingredients, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A pudding from the Cape served in a round bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: Zabaglione is an Italian sweet of whisked egg yolks, sugar and Marsala, served as a pudding.

clue.text: One's avarice has no end, yes?

parts.note: A is one, and the 's stands for has, linking to the next piece

indicators.note: having no end means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: greed is avarice

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question: is a person's lust for money limitless?
explanation.definitionFit: To agree is to say yes to something, so the question asks whether it is a yes.

clue.text: Author kept spinning plate

indicators.note: spinning turns something around, so the word is reversed

parts.note: had means kept or held
an L-plate is the learner sign on a car, giving L

explanation.surface: A writer keeps a plate twirling.
explanation.walkthrough: An L-plate is the red L sign on a British learner driver's car.
explanation.definitionFit: Roald Dahl is a well-known writer of children's books and short stories, a famous British author.

clue.text: Art seldom ruined by him?

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked and broken up, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A great painter rarely produced anything poor.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a great painter of old rarely botched a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: An Old Master is a leading European painter from before about 1800, whose work is rarely spoiled.

clue.text: Traveller to welcome Terry inside

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the clue's own words, spanning two of them

explanation.surface: A wayfarer comes to greet a man called Terry indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet journeys through the solar system on a long orbit, so it is a heavenly traveller.

clue.text: Excellent! McCartney's being broadcast

indicators.note: a broadcast is heard, so the answer is spelt as the name sounds

parts.note: Stella McCartney is the fashion designer, daughter of Paul McCartney

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic cry as a McCartney is put on the air.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent the name STELLA is pronounced exactly like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Stellar means starry, and informally outstanding, so as an exclamation it praises something superb.

clue.text: Regular beans with poor diet wants a vitamin! Tempted?

indicators.note: regular letters are every other one, so the second and fourth of the word are taken
a poor version is badly made, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written
the diet wants vitamin C, so the letter C joins the letters of diet

explanation.surface: Someone living on beans and a bad diet needs a vitamin; are they lured by a supplement?
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges DIET together with the C it wants, giving TICED.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or attract someone, so enticed is a synonym of tempted in the past tense.
